title: Personalized hidden Markov model reveals Alzheimer disease progression states
summary: A personalized hidden Markov model trained on ADNI longitudinal multimodal data (1,192 impaired participants, 388 controls) identified ten disease-related states in three stages and two progression patterns. Using the state index to predict time to dementia, it reached a C-index of 0.923 versus 0.774 for hippocampal volume and 0.808 for MMSE. External validation used AIBL (87 impaired, 179 controls), but its numbers are not in the abstract; this is a version 1 preprint.
ai_technology: Personalized hidden Markov model on longitudinal multimodal data identifying disease-related states

evidence.tested: Train, validation and test on ADNI with external validation in AIBL; retrospective analysis of prospective cohorts.
evidence.unknown: External-validation performance, clinical use of the states and generality; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Infers disease states and progression patterns used for prognosis.

source_review.scope: Version 1 abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations from Europe PMC or Crossref. Full text not accessed.
